dmm-2017-power-01.prompt: There are six people at a party. For every pair of them, they are either friends or strangers. Prove that either there are three people all of whom are friends with each other, or there are three people no two of whom are friends. (Hint: show that there is someone who has either three friends or three strangers among the others.)
dmm-2017-power-01.answer: Proof (see solution): pigeonhole on one person's five relationships.

dmm-2017-power-02.prompt:
Throughout, a *graph* $G=(V,E)$ has a vertex set $V$ and an edge set $E$ of unordered pairs of distinct vertices; $K_n$ is the complete graph on $n$ vertices. A *red-blue coloring* colors every edge red or blue, and a complete subgraph is *monochromatic* if all its edges have one color. The *Ramsey number* $R(s,t)$ is the smallest $n$ such that every red-blue coloring of $K_n$ contains a red $K_s$ or a blue $K_t$.

Suppose $V$ is a vertex set with $|V|=n$ and $K_n=(V,E_K)$ is the complete graph on $V$. Show that there is a one-to-one correspondence between subgraphs $G=(V,E\subseteq E_K)$ of $K_n$ on the vertex set $V$ and red-blue colorings $c$ of the edges of $K_n$.
dmm-2017-power-02.answer: The map $c\mapsto(V,\{e: c(e)=\text{red}\})$ is a bijection.

dmm-2017-power-03a.prompt:

A *red-blue coloring* colors every edge red or blue, and a complete subgraph is *monochromatic* if all its edges have one color. The *Ramsey number* $R(s,t)$ is the smallest $n$ such that every red-blue coloring of $K_n$ contains a red $K_s$ or a blue $K_t$.

Given $s\in\mathbb N$, prove that $R(2,s)=s$.
dmm-2017-power-03a.answer: Every coloring of $K_s$ has a red edge ($K_2$ red) or is entirely blue ($K_s$ blue); $K_{s-1}$ all blue is a counterexample for $n=s-1$.

dmm-2017-power-03b.answer: Swapping the two colors turns colorings with no red $K_s$/blue $K_t$ into colorings with no red $K_t$/blue $K_s$.

dmm-2017-power-04a.answer: Color the $5$-cycle edges red and the $5$ diagonals blue.

dmm-2017-power-05a.answer: Restrict the coloring to any $R(s,t)$ vertices.

dmm-2017-power-05c.answer: Induct on $s+t$ using the recursive inequality.

The figure shows a graph on $8$ vertices placed around a circle (solid lines are viewed as red edges, and all pairs of vertices that are not joined are blue edges); it shows that $R(3,4)>8$. By extending this construction, show that $R(3,s+1)>3s-1$ for all integers $s\ge2$.
dmm-2017-power-06a.answer: Circulant coloring on $\mathbb Z_{3s-1}$: red if the difference is in $\{s,\dots,2s-1\}$ (mod $3s-1$).

dmm-2017-power-06b.prompt:

dmm-2017-power-06b.answer: A coloring of $K_9$ with no red $K_3$ and no blue $K_4$ would force every vertex to have red degree $3$, giving $27/2$ red edges.

dmm-2017-power-07.prompt:

Consider the graph with vertex set $\mathbb Z_{17}$ (the integers modulo $17$) in which the pair $\{i,j\}$ is an edge (red) if and only if $i-j\equiv\pm1,\pm2,\pm4,\pm8\pmod{17}$, and a non-edge (blue) otherwise. By considering this coloring of $K_{17}$, show that $R(4,4)=18$. (You may use $R(3,4)=9$ and the inequality $R(s,t)\le R(s-1,t)+R(s,t-1)$.)
dmm-2017-power-07.answer: Lower bound: the quadratic-residue coloring of $K_{17}$ has no monochromatic $K_4$; upper bound: $R(4,4)\le2R(3,4)=18$.

dmm-2017-power-08a.prompt: For $r\ge2$ and $s_1,\dots,s_r\in\mathbb N$, the *generalized Ramsey number* $R_r(s_1,\dots,s_r)$ is the smallest $n$ such that for every coloring of the edges of $K_n$ with $r$ colors $1,\dots,r$ there is a complete subgraph $K_{s_j}$ all of whose edges have color $j$, for some $j$. In particular $R_2(s_1,s_2)=R(s_1,s_2)$. Show that $$R_r(s_1,s_2,\dots,s_r)\le R_{r-1}\big(R(s_1,s_2),s_3,\dots,s_r\big).$$
dmm-2017-power-08a.answer: Merge colors 1 and 2 into one color.
